text:
Maya R: Heads up — customer on private VPC in eu-west-2 reports sudden NCCL timeouts and degraded throughput after a routine OS/kernel patch yesterday. Logs show repeated "NCCL WARN net: connection timed out" from a subset of nodes.

Jordan P: Oof. Which image/kernel did they bump to? Any change to the GPU driver meanwhile?

Maya R: Customer says kernel moved from 5.15.0-70 -> 5.15.0-88 and the instance image applied a vendor kernel patch. They claim driver stayed at 535.86, but we see processes failing with GPU link errors.

Lee S: Can we get `uname -a` + `modinfo nvidia` + `nvidia-smi -q` from an affected node? Also `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` and `journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -n 200`.

Maya R: Pasted sample from one host: ```
uname -a
Linux gpu-node-12 5.15.0-88-generic #89~vendor SMP Mon Mar 1 04:12:23 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux

modinfo nvidia | head -n3
filename: /lib/modules/5.15.0-88/updates/nvidia.ko
version: 535.86
srcversion: ABCDE123456

nvidia-smi -q | grep -E "Driver Version|CUDA Version"
Driver Version : 535.86
CUDA Version : 12.2
```

Lee S: Looks pinned superficially but vendor kernel modules could be ABI-mismatched. If DKMS rebuilt against a slightly different toolchain or the kernel introduced a new Kconfig for NUMA/PCIE patches, the ABI can subtly change and NC L multipath gets unhappy.

Camille Ops: Customer also reported intermittent RX/TX drops in the VPC overlay; might be MTU/encap changes in that kernel. NCCL is sensitive to socket behavior. Can we collect `ethtool -k` and `ip route show table all`?

Jordan P: Also ask them for `cat /sys/module/nvidia/version` and `ls -l /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/updates/ | grep nvidia`. Sometimes vendor packages drop a different .ko and the system ends up loading the wrong module from an older kernel tree.

Maya R: I requested the extra outputs. They attached a short dmesg dump showing `NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: failed to init NVML: Unknown error -6` and some `vfio` notices around the same time.

Lee S: Unknown error -6 (NVML) often maps to an ABI mismatch or missing kernel symbols. Two high-likelihood causes: 1) vendor kernel recompiled nvidia.ko with incompatible compiler flags, or 2) kernel changed some PCI/ASPM/PCIe ASPM policy affecting peer-to-peer.

Camille Ops: Proposal: ask customer to (A) try booting a node into the older vendor kernel (5.15.0-70) to confirm regression, (B) if rollback not possible, load the driver from the initramfs that we ship (they can mount and `modprobe /path/to/nvidia.ko`) for a quick test. We'll need a maintenance window if we ask them to reboot.

Jordan P: Agreed. Also recommend they disable the vendor DKMS automatic rebuild and pin the nv driver package temporarily. We'll document exact commands. If rollback reproduces stable NCCL, it's a kernel-side regression and we escalate to the vendor.

Maya R: Customer is requesting guidance; they asked if Redwood supports kernels with vendor-specific patches in Private. Our matrix lists 5.15.x variants but not every vendor-patched build. They want a definitive statement.

Lee S: Short answer: we support driver X kernel matrix combinations we validate. Vendor-patched kernels are outside guaranteed matrix. We can triage but long-term they need to either stay on a validated kernel or move to Dedicated where we control AMI/kernel.

Camille Ops: I'll open a P1 ticket and note this as a compatibility claim against `linux 5.15.0-88~vendor`. Action items: (1) get rollback confirmation, (2) if rollback fixes it — update our compatibility matrix and add an advisory, (3) if rollback doesn't fix — capture full nv module build ID and escalate to driver team.

Maya R: Customer agreed to a rollback test at 02:00 UTC. I added the commands to our support doc.

deploy-bot: Canary health check detected higher NCCL latency on route `eu-west-2/private-gpu`. Rolling canary back to kernel 5.15.0-70 on 2/3 nodes. :information_desk_person:

Jordan P: If rollback fixes CANARY, schedule a controlled roll forward to reproduce and collect `perf top`, `tcpdump` on NCCL ports, and `nvidia-bug-report.sh` output. We need concrete artifacts for vendor bug.

Lee S: Also flag cost impact: if we need an expedited on-site field engineer for a customer datacenter (air-gapped on-prem), that's a separate billable line item. For cloud VPCs it's mostly engineering time and possible capacity churn.

Camille Ops: Ticket created: INF-2026-1142. I'll add follow-ups: matrix update, KB entry for pinning drivers, and a checklist for Private customers to prevent auto-kernel upgrades.

Maya R: Thanks — I'll update the customer thread after the 02:00 test. Will post results here. :eyes:
